title: Ask for changes to the draft
prompt:
# Story 4: Ask for changes to the draft

- **Story**: XXX-revise-enabler-draft
- **Created**: 2026-11-08
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: with a Ready draft, write "Add a task to verify the migration on an empty database", press Enter and see the whole draft written
  again with the change; ask again, and approve.

## Story

As a team member, I want to tell the AI what to change in the draft, in my own words, so that I get the enabler I mean before I approve it.

## Acceptance tests

- [ ] **Given** a draft that is Ready or Incomplete, **Then** the box says "Ask for changes to the draft...", the send button is named "Send
  changes", the ADR panel and the Link button are gone, and a line says "Revising the draft below".
- [ ] **Given** the user types a change and presses Enter (or the button), **Then** it shows as a message on the right, the draft chip
  reads "Writing...", and the card shows the new text as it arrives, in place of the old one.
- [ ] **Given** the reply, **Then** it is the **complete** revised document, not a difference. **When** it ends, **Then** the chip reads
  "Ready for review" and the card shows it.
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** the turns sent are the first request, the previous draft as the assistant's turn, and the change as the
  user's turn, as typed. Earlier revisions are in the turns too.
- [ ] **Given** a revision that failed, **Then** Retry sends the same turns again.
- [ ] **Given** a draft that is being written or has failed, **Then** a change cannot be sent (the box says why, as in story 2).
- [ ] **Given** a revision, **Then** the number, the slug, the planned path, the chosen ADRs and the links of the draft do not change.
- [ ] **Given** a draft revised twice, **Then** approving stores the last text, and the stored prompt is the first one.
- [ ] **Given** the conversation reaches 40 turns, **Then** the backend refuses the next change, and its error shows in the card with Retry.
- [ ] **Given** the user discards the draft, **Then** the box goes back to the prompt for a new enabler.
- [ ] **Given** the prompt cache, **Then** a point is set after the system prompt, after the project context, and after the previous draft, so
  that a revision reads most of its input from the cache. The token chips show it (story 2).

## Business rules and constraints

- A change is an instruction on the whole draft. The AI returns the whole document, keeps the identifier and the date, and changes only what
  was asked.
- A request carries at most 40 turns, alternating user and assistant, starting and ending with a user turn.
- The text of the user's change is sent as typed. The draft that is sent back is the one on screen, not an older one.

## Out of scope

- Changing the ADRs or the links of a draft (discard it and start again), going back to an earlier version of the draft, and comparing two
  versions.
- Asking for changes to an enabler that was approved (another story).

## Tasks

- [ ] Change the composer when there is a Ready or Incomplete draft: placeholder, button name, hidden panels, the "Revising" line.
- [ ] Add a user turn to the draft and run the request again, keeping the number, the slug, the ADRs and the links.
- [ ] Send the turns with the previous draft, and replace the card's text with the new one.
- [ ] Set the cache points on the system prompt, the context and the previous assistant turn in the backend call.
- [ ] Refuse more than 40 turns in the backend, with a clear message.
- [ ] Test with a fake backend: one revision, two, a failed one with Retry, and the turns that are sent.

tasks.text: Update the composer ViewModel to expose a `revisionMode` state that activates when the draft status is Ready or Incomplete, setting the placeholder text, button label, and visibility flags for the ADR panel and Link button

Add a `requestRevision(changeText: string)` command to the draft use case that appends a user turn and re-invokes the generation port, preserving the draft's identifier, slug, planned path, ADRs, and links
Update the draft card component to replace its displayed text in place as the revised stream arrives, reusing the streaming display established in story 025
Implement turn accumulation in the backend application service: build the full turn list (original prompt → previous draft → change → …) and pass it to the AI provider port
Add a cache-point instruction to the backend AI provider adapter after the system prompt, after the project context, and after the most recent assistant turn
Add a guard in the backend application service that rejects a revision request when the turn count would exceed 40, returning a descriptive error
Map the 40-turn error to an HTTP response in the inbound REST adapter and surface it in the draft card with a Retry option
Write ViewModel unit tests covering: entering revision mode, a successful single revision, two successive revisions, a failed revision followed by Retry, and discard returning to new-enabler state
Write a backend unit test verifying the exact turns sent for a first revision, a second revision, and the 40-turn rejection
